He played [[college basketball]] for [[New Mexico State University]] (NMSU).{{cite news |author1=Geoff Grammer |title=Lofton finds home at NMSU |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98170086/lofton-finds-home-at-nmsu/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Albuquerque Journal]] |date=9 December 2017 |page=D2|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} He transferred to NMSU from [[Texas Southern Tigers basketball|Texas Southern]], where he was named the [[Southwestern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Southwestern Athletic Conference Player of the Year]] in 2017.{{cite news |author1=C.J. Moore |title=CBB's Ultimate Journeyman Zach Lofton Finally Finds His Home |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2759136-cbbs-ultimate-journeyman-zach-lofton-finally-finds-his-home |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=15 February 2018}} He later played for other teams in different countries. ==College career== Lofton, a [[shooting guard]] from [[Saint Paul, Minnesota]], started his college career at [[San Jacinto College]], then played his sophomore season for [[Illinois State University]]. He averaged 11.3 points per game for the Redbirds before transferring to Minnesota in 2014. While sitting out his transfer year, Lofton was dismissed from the Golden Gophers team before playing a game.{{cite magazine|last1=Axson|first1=Scooby|title=Minnesota dismisses transfer guard Zach Lofton|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2014/10/30/minnesota-zach-lofton-dismissed|access-date=June 5, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 30, 2014}}{{cite news|last1=Rayno|first1=Amelia|title=Transfer Zach Lofton kicked off Gophers basketball team|url=http://www.startribune.com/transfer-zach-lofton-kicked-off-gophers-basketball-team/280870422/|access-date=June 5, 2017|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=October 30, 2014|archive-date=March 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328112405/http://www.startribune.com/transfer-zach-lofton-kicked-off-gophers-basketball-team/280870422/|url-status=dead}} Lofton landed at Texas Southern, where in [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17]] he averaged 16.8 points per game and led the Tigers to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2017 NCAA tournament]]. At the close of the season, he was named SWAC Player of the Year and Newcomer of the Year.{{cite news|title=2016-17 All-SWAC Men's Basketball Teams announced|url=http://www.swac.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=27400&ATCLID=211515505|access-date=June 5, 2017|work=[[Southwestern Athletic Conference]]|date=March 6, 2017}} Following his lone season with Texas Southern, Lofton declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]]. Although he ultimately withdrew, he did announce that he would transfer from Texas Southern.{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Texas Southern's Zach Lofton to transfer|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/05/01/texas-southerns-zach-lofton-to-transfer/|access-date=June 5, 2017|work=[[NBCSports.com]]|date=May 1, 2017}} He ultimately chose [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] to play his final season of college eligibility.{{cite news|last1=Rudi|first1=Mark|title=Texas Southern grad transfer Zach Lofton signs with NMSU|url=http://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/nmsu/2017/07/03/texas-southern-grad-transfer-zach-lofton-signs-nmsu/448952001/|access-date=July 3, 2017|work=[[Las Cruces Sun-News]]|date=July 3, 2017}} As a senior at New Mexico State, Lofton averaged 20.1 points and 5.0 rebounds per game. He shot 46 percent from the field and 38 percent from behind the arc. Lofton was named to the All-[[Western Athletic Conference]] First Team and the 2018 All-WAC Newcomer team. Following the season he participated in the 2018 [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]].{{cite news|last1=Rudi|first1=Mark|title=New Mexico State's Zach Lofton invited to play in Portsmouth Invitational|url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/blogs/off-the-mark/2018/04/09/new-mexico-states-zach-lofton-invited-play-portsmouth-invitational/500285002/|access-date=April 17, 2018|work=[[Las Cruces Sun News]]|date=April 9, 2018}} ==Professional career== Lofton was not selected in the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite news |author1=Vince Ellis |title=Zach Attack |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98170604/zach-attack/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=18 October 2018 |pages=C1, C6|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} He signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]] for the NBA Summer League.{{cite news |title=Zach Lofton to play for Detroit Pistons Summer League team |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/blogs/off-the-mark/2018/06/24/zach-lofton-play-detroit-pistons-summer-league-team/727354002/ |access-date=June 25, 2018 |work=[[Las Cruces Sun-News]] |date=June 24, 2018}} He averaged 10.8 points and 2.5 rebounds per game and scored 21 points in the final Summer League game against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Lofton subsequently signed with the Pistons{{cite news |last1=Rudi |first1=Mark |title=Former New Mexico State Aggie Zach Lofton signs with Detroit Pistons |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/2018/08/11/former-new-mexico-state-aggie-zach-lofton-signs-detroit-pistons/968308002/ |access-date=September 26, 2018 |work=[[Las Cruces Sun-News]] |date=August 11, 2018}} and, in October, agreed to a [[two-way contract]], splitting playing time with the Pistons and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24993789/pistons-exercise-2-way-conversion-option-zach-lofton |title=Pistons exercise 2-way conversion option on Zach Lofton |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=October 15, 2018 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=October 15, 2018}} On October 17, 2018, Lofton made his NBA debut with the Pistons. He recorded one steal in four minutes of play in a 103–100 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20181017/BKNDET#/boxscore |title=Archived copy |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 18, 2018 |archive-date=October 18, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181018082930/https://www.nba.com/games/20181017/BKNDET#/boxscore |url-status=dead }} In his G League debut, Lofton had a double-double with 26 points, 11 rebounds, nine assists and four steals as the Drive lost to the [[Erie BayHawks (2017–)|Erie BayHawks]] 125–114.{{cite web |title=Bayhawks stop Drive |url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20181102/GRDERI/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 4, 2018}} On January 15, 2019, Lofton was waived by the Pistons, but retained by the Drive.{{cite news|title=Zach Lofton: Let go by Pistons|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/zach-lofton-let-go-by-detroit/|access-date=January 17, 2019|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=January 15, 2019}} He averaged 13.3 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.3 assists, and 1.2 steals per game with the Drive. On February 1, 2020, Lofton signed with the [[Rostock Seawolves]] of the German [[ProA]] league.{{cite news |title=SEAWOLVES verpflichten Ex-NBA-Profi Zach Lofton |url=https://seawolves.de/2020/02/seawolves-verpflichten-ex-nba-profi-zach-lofton/ |website=[[Rostock Seawolves]] |access-date=October 16, 2020 |language=de |date=February 1, 2020}} He averaged 27.7 points, 4.7 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game. On July 18, 2021, Lofton signed with [[Kazma SC (basketball)|Kazma]] of the Kuwaiti Division I Basketball League.{{cite web |last1=Madwar |first1=Ahmad |title=Kazma sign a second import player, ex Rostock |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/694984/Kazma-sign-a-second-import-player,-ex-Rostock |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=July 18, 2021}} On September 22, 2022,
